what_its_for: Evolocumab is used to lower your LDL ('bad') cholesterol levels in your blood. It is used in adults who have high cholesterol that has not been controlled well enough with diet changes and statin medicines (like atorvastatin or simvastatin). It is also used to lower the risk of heart attack, stroke, and certain heart procedures in people who already have heart disease. In some cases, it is used to treat a rare inherited condition called homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, which causes very high cholesterol from birth.
how_to_take: Evolocumab is given as a shot (injection) under the skin (subcutaneous). You will inject it into the upper arm, thigh, or belly (abdomen), but NOT into areas where the skin is tender, bruised, red, or hard. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to give yourself the injection. Always rotate the injection site each time so you are not using the same spot. The medicine comes as a prefilled autoinjector pen or a prefilled syringe, making it easier to give yourself at home. Let the medicine warm up at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before injecting — do NOT warm it in a microwave or hot water.
dosing: The usual dose depends on why you are taking the medicine. For lowering cholesterol or reducing heart disease risk: 140 mg injected every 2 weeks, OR 420 mg injected once a month. The 420 mg monthly dose requires either three 140 mg injections given one after another within 30 minutes, or a single 420 mg prefilled cartridge used with the Pushtronex system. For homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: 420 mg once a month. Your doctor will decide which dose and schedule is right for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is more than 7 days away. If your next dose is within 7 days, skip the missed dose and give your next injection on the regularly scheduled day. Then continue your normal schedule. Do not give two injections at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store evolocumab in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original box to protect it from light. Do NOT freeze it — throw it away if it has been frozen. If needed, you can store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 30 days. Once kept at room temperature, do not put it back in the refrigerator. Throw it away if it has been at room temperature for more than 30 days. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used pens or syringes in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Do not inject into skin that is sore, red, bruised, tattooed, or scarred. Do not shake the autoinjector or syringe. Do not freeze the medication. Avoid skipping doses, as consistent use is important for keeping your cholesterol under control. Continue following your heart-healthy, low-fat, low-cholesterol diet while using this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek medical help right away if you experience: serious allergic reactions such as rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; injection site reactions that are severe, do not go away, or become infected (redness, pain, swelling, or a lump at the injection site that worsens); confusion, memory problems, or difficulty thinking clearly; muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness (especially if you also take a statin). Also call your doctor if your cholesterol levels do not improve or if you have any concerns about your treatment.
when_it_works: Evolocumab starts working quickly — it begins lowering your LDL ('bad') cholesterol within a few days of your first injection. You may see the full effect on your cholesterol levels within 4 to 8 weeks. Your doctor will check your cholesterol with blood tests to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep using the medicine even if you feel fine, because high cholesterol usually has no symptoms.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not fully known if evolocumab is safe during pregnancy or passes into breast milk. Your doctor will help you decide if the benefits outweigh any risks. Children: Evolocumab is approved for use in children (ages 10 and older) with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your doctor may monitor you more closely. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but always mention all other medicines you are taking to your doctor.
